correctness.rationale: For nonzero UQNA S, Hahn--Banach support at its distinguished u and a UQNA norming subsequence show ||y* S||=||S||. Every maximizing sequence for the real part of y*S has images converging to u because the support functional forces the unique unimodular phase. The ell_1(Gamma) coefficient truncations a_n and any disjoint tail witnesses z_n make both a_n+z_n and a_n-z_n maximizing; hence Sz_n->0. Contradiction to nonuniform tail norm proves ||S(I-P_Fn)||->0 and therefore compactness. The zero case and uncountable Gamma are included. Corollary 3.11(a) of arXiv:2004.11025v1 supplies reverse density; weakly null unit vectors give identity essential norm exactly 1. All critical quantifiers and real/complex phases were checked analytically; no finite computations serve as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The 2020 primary paper introduces UQNA, proves density within the compact ideal, and only bounds the distance of the identity on c0 away from zero using a 1/4 threshold. The 2025 RSE paper controls an explicitly stronger intersection class, not UQNA without norm attainment. The new proof forces arbitrary UQNA operators on c0(Gamma) to be compact and consequently identifies an entire closure and all distances to it; targeted indexed searches found no covering result. Residual risk of unindexed equivalent work is acknowledged.

value.rationale: The source identifies a concrete failure of UQNA density for the identity c0, with only a 1/4 obstruction. The new structural theorem identifies the entire norm closure as the compact ideal for arbitrary targets and index sets, yields exact distances to the UQNA class for all operators, and sharpens the identity obstruction to 1. Its mechanism explains why this uniqueness notion forbids noncompact tail action despite not requiring an attained norm. This is a natural complete operator-ideal classification, not a textbook scalar deduction or arbitrary example.
